shadow_trades.reasoning_summary: Starting from an even bundle (A=1, B=1, C=1), trading 1 A for 1 B changes my inventory to A=0, B=2, C=1, which reduces variety. Since I value goods equally and prefer balancing lower-count goods, this trade lowers my utility.
I currently hold one of each good, so my bundle is perfectly balanced. Trading 1×B for 1×A would make my inventory less varied (A:2, B:0, C:1), which lowers utility under my preference for variety.
Trading 1 B for 2 A increases my total goods, and after the trade I still keep variety across all three goods while gaining more overall value.
Starting from an even 1A, 1B, 1C bundle, trading 1C for 1B would create an imbalanced inventory (A:1, B:2, C:0). Since I value goods equally and prefer variety, this reduces my utility.
Starting from an even bundle of A, B, and C, trading 1 B for 1 C would reduce variety and leave me with no B, so it lowers my utility.

Giving 1 B and receiving 2 C changes my inventory from (A1,B1,C1) to (A1,B0,C3). Since all goods are valued equally but I prefer variety, this reduces variety and makes my holdings more imbalanced, so it does not increase my utility.
I value all goods equally and currently have one of each, so trading 1×A for 1×B would reduce variety by leaving me with no A and extra B, lowering my utility.
Trading 1×B for 1×A would change my balanced inventory from (A:1, B:1, C:1) to (A:2, B:0, C:1), reducing variety. Since I value the goods equally and prefer a more even mix, this lowers my utility.
Giving 1 B and receiving 2 A increases my total goods, and after the trade my bundle becomes more balanced in value overall despite having less variety.
With one of each good, my bundle is perfectly balanced. Trading 1×C for 1×B would make my inventory less varied (B:2, C:0, A:1), which lowers utility.
Starting from an even bundle of A, B, and C, trading 1 B for 1 C would make my inventory less balanced (A:1, B:0, C:2). Since I value variety, this reduces my utility.
Giving 1 B and receiving 2 C changes my inventory from (1,1,1) to (0,3,1). Since all goods are valued equally and this increases my total goods by 1, it improves my bundle despite reducing variety.

Trading 1 A for 1 B improves my variety by turning my scarcest good from 0 B to 1 B, while reducing a more abundant good from 2 A to 1 A. The resulting bundle is more balanced, and B is also currently harder to obtain.
This trade increases variety by converting surplus A into scarce B. Moving from A=2, B=0, C=2 to A=0, B=1, C=2 better balances my inventory, and B is currently harder to obtain.
Trading 1 C for 1 B improves variety in my inventory: I currently have no B and extra C, and B is also scarce in the market.
This trade improves my variety: I currently have no B and extra C, and B is also becoming harder to obtain. Moving from (B0,C2,A2) to (B1,C0,A2) better balances my holdings and increases utility.

Trading 1 A for 1 B increases variety in my inventory, changing it from A2/B0/C2 to A1/B1/C2. Since I value goods equally but prefer goods I have less of, gaining scarce B improves my bundle. The market also indicates B is harder to obtain, which further supports accepting.

This trade increases variety in my inventory by turning surplus A into scarce B. Moving from (A2, B0, C2) to (A0, B1, C2) gives me access to a good I currently lack, and B is also harder to obtain in the market.

Trading 1 C for 1 B improves my variety by changing my inventory from A2/B0/C2 to A2/B1/C1, which better matches my preference for balanced holdings. The market also indicates B is harder to obtain, increasing the value of receiving B now.
This trade increases variety by turning surplus C into scarce B. My inventory would shift from (A2, B0, C2) to (A2, B1, C0), which better balances my bundle, and B is currently harder to obtain.

Starting from an even bundle of 1A, 1B, 1C, trading 1A for 1B gives me 0A, 2B, 1C, which reduces variety. The market says B is scarcer, but I only accept trades that increase my utility, and this trade makes my holdings less balanced.

I currently have one of each good, which is ideal for variety. Trading away 1×B for 1×A would leave me with fewer B and extra A, reducing variety. B also appears harder to obtain in the market, making it especially costly to give up now.
Giving up my only B is unattractive because B is currently scarce and valuable in the market, and this trade would reduce my variety from one of each good to no B at all.

Trading 1 C for 1 B changes my inventory from (A1,B1,C1) to (A1,B2,C0). Since B is currently harder to obtain and in higher demand, receiving B for C improves the value of my bundle enough to justify the loss of variety.

Starting from a perfectly balanced bundle (1A, 1B, 1C), trading away 1B for 1C would reduce variety and leave me with no B. Since B is also currently harder to obtain, this does not improve my utility.
